description: The coupled bout with CaMKK2 knocked out (kCaMKK = 0, the authors' own surgery). Identical calcium and demand to ampk_francis_soce_on; whatever separates the two is what the calcium arm was doing. The paper's Figure 8C: exercise-induced AMPK activity depends strongly on CaMKK2.

protocol.francis_protocol: THEIRS: expt 3 (SOCE on), 0.1625 s of 100 Hz stimulation per 0.65 s stride -- this paper's own methods, p.17, and Francis et al.'s Figure 8C caption. OURS: the length. We run 10 strides, 6.5 s of exercise then 6.5 s of recovery; the published length for this stimulus is 60 s ('repeated for a total of 60 seconds') and no published run of either paper holds a recovery segment.
protocol.parameters: nominal_params, unmodified except the knockout above

provenance.archive_version: github:natejlinden/AMPK@71513c063dee2e985c024099f44586be403dfc7d (branch rev1, the branch the published figures were produced on; `main` stops before the code behind Figs 6-9).
provenance.exported_copy: NOT THE ARCHIVE. Samples were dropped, never interpolated or smoothed, so this copy does not contain all of the archive's turning points: ATP_hydrolysis_total peaks at 1.848 here against 1.868 in the archive (1.36% of its range). Every claim above is the archive's and is unedited; this line is what the export did to the numbers those claims are about. `sampling` says the stride and the rounding.
provenance.fitted_to: AMPK biosensor recordings, not exercise and not muscle fibres. The authors estimated the kinetic parameters against cytosolic AMPK activity measured with ExRai-AMPKAR (Schmitt et al., Nat Commun 13:3856, 2022), under a 2-deoxyglucose stimulus they model by cutting glycolytic ATP production 100-fold, 0.5 to 0.005 per s. Applying the fitted model to exercise is the authors' own extension, driven by Francis et al.'s calcium and ATP hydrolysis. The cell type behind those recordings is not stated in the preprint and is not guessed here. Which human muscle this run is shown under is OURS: a navigation choice, not a claim about that muscle. The authors' own reference list includes McConell et al., 'Skeletal Muscle AMPK Is Not Activated during 2 h of Moderate Intensity Exercise at ~65% in Endurance Trained Men'.
provenance.input_scale_note: Peak prescribed calcium is 29.8 uM against the 0.25 uM the 2-DG scenarios use, and the RHS takes calcium cubed (JCa = kOnCaM*Ca**3*CaM). The coupled scenarios therefore drive the calcium arm far outside the range the published sensitivity analysis explored. Stated, not corrected: feeding the file's uM column straight in is what the authors' own interface does.

provenance.integrator: SciPy solve_ivp(method='LSODA') at the authors' rtol=atol=1e-6 — NOT diffrax Kvaerno5 with a PID controller, which needs jax and is not installed here. Checked: tightening to rtol=1e-8/atol=1e-10 moves ATP at the end of the coupled bout by 2e-6 relative and the sensor ratio by 1e-8.
provenance.known_discrepancy: Table 13's last four rows are mislabelled upstream — the sampling script and the analysis script carry different free-parameter orders and SALib indexes by column. Reported in validation/REPORT.md, paper 2 §3; it changes which parameter is called quiet, not any trajectory here.
provenance.model_version: Model 6, MM_nonessential_all — the full non-essential-activation model. RHS executed from the authors' own bytes (sha256 384aadba41e2bb7e…), nominal_params and init_conds loaded from MM_nonessential_all.json unmodified.

series_defined_by_us.ATP_hydrolysis_total: OURS, and the only exported series that is an INPUT to the AMPK model rather than a state of it: the ATP hydrolysis rate the integrator was driven by, as generated: 0.3779 mM/s at the rest floor, rising once per repetition. EVERY EXPORTED GRID UNDERSAMPLES THE PEAK and none of them may be read for it: the stimulus is 100 Hz, this archive samples at 154 Hz and its column tops out at 1.8683 mM/s, 0.8% under the input's own 2 kHz value; the app copy is thinned further and is lower again. Stated rather than corrected — interpolating the spike back up would invent a value the model never integrated. It is Francis et al. output through our validated port, on OUR ten-repetition protocol, divided by 1000 the way exercise.ipynb cell 9 divides theirs — the file is uM/s and the right-hand side wants mM/s. QUOTED AND NOT OURS: Linden-Santangeli et al. report AMPK activation beginning between 2.0 and 5.0 mM/s. The bout's peak demand is 1.88256 mM/s, below the low edge — THIS is the number to print against that threshold. It is a statement about this protocol, not about resistance exercise.
series_defined_by_us.CaMKK_active_fraction: OURS. CaMKK_act / (CaMKK + CaMKK_act). The authors plot CaMKK_act itself (exercise.ipynb cell 19) on an axis labelled mM; the same notebook labels the pAMPK activity axis mM/s in one cell and uM/s in the next, so their own labels do not agree and we do not adopt either.
series_defined_by_us.pAMPK_fraction: OURS. Sum of the authors' AMPK_IDX phosphorylated members (pAMPK, AMP_pAMPK, ADP_pAMPK, ATP_pAMPK) over the whole conserved AMPK pool. The pool and its conservation are the authors'; expressing it as a fraction is ours, and it is done because the archive states no concentration unit for the protein species.

stands_in_for.measured_difference: Their resistance input runs 60 s with the bout in the first 3.25 s (exercise.ipynb cell 5 shades 0-3.25); ours runs 13.0 s with a 6.5 s bout.
stands_in_for.missing_artifact: 20250525_Francis_et_al/resistance_data.txt and running_data.txt, read by exercise.ipynb cell 3 and present on no branch of the pinned clone.
stands_in_for.what_is_ours: The CALCIUM TRACE is ours end to end: our run of our validated port of Francis et al. The STIMULUS SHAPE is the authors' and is published — preprint p.17, 0.1625 s of 100 Hz activation per 0.65 s stride — and we use it, for 13.0 s against their 60. What was never published is the two output files exercise.ipynb reads and which expt produced them, so this is NOT a reconstruction of those files and must not be renamed into one. NOT the authors' file.

provenance.uncertainty: NONE SHIPS. The authors' exercise figure is a 50-sample posterior ensemble drawn from results/param_est/.../Pathfinder.nc, which is absent from every branch of the pinned clone. One nominal-parameter trajectory ships instead. Do not read the single line as a posterior mean and do not draw a band around it.
provenance.validation: WHAT IS CHECKED IS THE MODEL, NOT THIS RUN. Supplemental Table 13 reproduces 72/72 cells exact at 3 decimal places (max |delta| 4.8e-4), which checks the right-hand side and the nominal parameters. But that table is a Sobol analysis computed over the authors' 2-DG protocol, and THIS SCENARIO DOES NOT RUN IT. Nothing published covers this protocol: no trajectory to check the curve against, and no sensitivity indices over the range it drives. See input_scale_note - the calcium here runs far outside the range that analysis explored.
provenance.whose_protocol: shape the authors' (exercise.ipynb cell 7); input file and Francis protocol ours

sampling.note: the first `head_samples` archived samples, then every `stride`th, rounded. No interpolation or smoothing, and the resulting grid is NOT uniform — search `t`.
